title: Instrumentation
tagline: Measurement and uncertainty, sensors, bridges, signal conditioning, data acquisition and EMC
summary: Engineering depends on measuring things accurately. This course treats measurement errors and uncertainty, sensors and transducers, bridges and signal conditioning, instrumentation amplifiers, grounding and shielding, data acquisition, test instruments and electromagnetic compatibility.
overview: The instrument, and the one that the signal is for, is the one that the limit is for, and the one that the error is for. This course follows the measurement from the signal and the error to the uncertainty and the one that the design is for, and gives the method and the check that make it work.
We build the instrument from the signal and the error, and then study how we measure the limit and the one that the signal is for.
outcomes: Describe the measurement, and the one that the error is for, of the signal and the limit
Describe the signal conditioning, and the one that the limit is for, in the instrument
Describe the acquisition, and the one that the number is for, in the code
Describe the electromagnetic compatibility, and the one that the time is for

chapters.title: Measurement and uncertainty

chapters.title: Sensors and transducers
chapters.summary: Resistive, capacitive, inductive, piezoelectric, thermal and optical sensors.

chapters.title: Bridges and signal conditioning
chapters.summary: Wheatstone and AC bridges, amplification, filtering, linearisation and excitation.

chapters.title: Instrumentation amplifiers, grounding and shielding
chapters.summary: Instrumentation amplifiers, common-mode rejection, ground loops, shielding and isolation.

chapters.title: Data acquisition
chapters.summary: Anti-aliasing, sampling, multiplexing and ADC selection in data-acquisition systems.

chapters.title: Test instruments
chapters.summary: Multimeters, oscilloscopes, spectrum analysers, signal generators and network analysers.

chapters.title: Electromagnetic compatibility
chapters.summary: Sources and coupling of interference, emissions and immunity, filtering, layout and EMC standards.
